bullets.title: AVGO: FY28 AI revenue guidance doubles to ~$230B; Anthropic/OpenAI become largest XPU customers
bullets.body: Broadcom F3Q26 beat (revenue $29.59B, EPS $3.32 vs. $3.22 consensus) but Q4 guidance of $34.8B slightly disappointed some. The major catalyst: management guided FY27 AI revenue to $115B (from $100B) and FY28 to ~$230B, implying 100%+ growth in each year. Anthropic becomes largest XPU customer in FY27 (~5GW then 10GW in FY28); OpenAI Jalapeño ramp adds 1.3GW in FY27. Citi raised PT to $515 (19x FY28 EPS of $30), UBS maintains Buy at $470, Wolfe reiterates Outperform at $500. Key risk: GOOGL shifting some TPU work to MediaTek/MRVL, though AVGO retains multi-year take-or-pay LTA covering tens of billions annually.

bullets.title: SNOW: Third straight quarter of product revenue acceleration; AI products drive path to 40%+ growth
bullets.body: Snowflake F2Q27 product revenue of $1.49B (+37% YoY) beat consensus by ~$72M (5%+). FY27 product revenue guidance raised to $6.07B (+36%) from prior +31%. Q3 guide implies +37-38% YoY, with management implying 40%+ exit rate into FY28. Cortex Code (CoCo) accounts reached 9,100+ with AI contributing roughly half of acceleration alongside core migrations. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.62 beat by $0.17. Key concern: product gross margin guided down to 74% (from 75%) as AI workloads carry lower margins; FCF conversion lagging. Citi upgraded to Buy with $490 PT; UBS raised PT to $500; Wolfe raised to $500.

bullets.title: DELL: Blowout quarter; AI server revenue guidance raised to $74B for FY27 with $95B backlog
bullets.body: Dell F2Q27 revenues of $47.0B (+58% YoY) crushed guidance of $44-45B; EPS of $7.04 beat $4.91 consensus. AI server revenue hit $16.4B (+100% YoY) with record $60.9B orders and $95B backlog. FY27 revenue guidance raised to $192B from $167B; EPS raised to $25.50 vs. prior $17.90. Traditional server revenue grew 122% YoY. Citi raised PT to $600 (Buy), JPM raised PT to $635 (OW). Bears note margin durability risk when memory prices normalize and enterprise spending plateaus.

bullets.title: CIEN: Strong F3Q26 beat; FY27 guidance implies 30%+ growth floor with $10B+ backlog
bullets.body: Ciena reported Q3 revenue of $1.67B and EPS of $2.11, beating consensus of $1.64B/$1.73 by comfortable margins. Gross margin of 46.4% vs. 45.0% expected. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 'at least' 30% with gross margins 45-46% and operating margins 25-27%—well above prior consensus. Backlog reached $8.5B with $10B+ targeted by year-end; supply constraints remain the gating factor through 2027-2028. Hyper-Rail ramping to several hundred million in FY27. Wolfe raised PT to $660 with 107% upside; JPM trimmed to $605 but reiterated OW; MS cut to $425 (EW) on supply/margin concerns.

bullets.title: ADBE: CEO succession—Anil Chakravarthy named next CEO; bears and bulls diverge on strategic direction
bullets.body: Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy (President of Customer Experience Orchestration) as CEO effective December 1, 2026, with Shantanu Narayen becoming Executive Chair. The appointment of an internal candidate disappointed some investors expecting external transformation. ADBE faces ongoing Creative Cloud headwinds from AI competition (Canva, Figma) while Digital Experience accelerates. KeyBanc maintains Underweight at $195 PT on decelerating revenues and AI threats; Citi Neutral at $301; Wolfe Peer Perform. ADBE reports earnings September 10 with consensus EPS $6.08, revenue $6.69B.

bullets.title: ORCL: Tactically attractive into F1Q27 earnings; OCI capacity at 63% YoY growth toward guidance
bullets.body: Oracle reports F1Q27 earnings September 10 (consensus $1.73 EPS, $19.13B revenue). The stock is down 25%+ since Q4 as capex/OCI ramp concerns weigh. MS raised PT to $210 on GPUaaS trajectory; KeyBanc OW at $300 PT citing 119% OCI revenue growth path; Citi TMT flags it as top conference idea. ORCL's $115B+ AI backlog (with OpenAI as major tenant) frames multi-year upside, but execution on cloud apps stability and margin expansion are key debates.

bullets.title: NVDA: Acquires Hugging Face for ~$12.9B; Vera Rubin CPX revived with HBM4; MediaTek $3.5B investment
bullets.body: Nvidia confirmed a definitive agreement to acquire Hugging Face for ~$11.9B plus $1B employee retention (total ~$12.9B), expected to close H1 2027. The deal secures NVDA control over the leading open-source AI platform and 18M+ developers. Separately, NVDA invested $3.5B in MediaTek convertible bonds and deepened NVLink Fusion partnership—a competitive move seen as pressuring AVGO's custom ASIC dominance. Rubin CPX (with HBM4) confirmed in Q1 2027 production. US model release cadence accelerated to 12.5/quarter, a key driver of NVDA's datacenter revenue model.

bullets.title: MDB: Atlas holds 29% growth for fifth consecutive quarter; EA/Other emerges as second growth engine
bullets.body: MongoDB F2Q27 revenue of $771.8M (+30.5% YoY) beat $735M consensus; EPS of $1.90 beat $1.62. Atlas grew 29% YoY (record $127M net new quarterly revenue). Enterprise Advanced surged 36% YoY with AI workloads (Vector Search, Search) driving platform attach from 37% to 45%. FY27 guidance raised to $2.99-3.03B. Stock sold off -12-14% post-earnings as buyside expected 30%+ Atlas and softer H2 deceleration guidance raised concerns. Citi raised PT to $565 (Buy); Wolfe raised to $500 (Outperform) framing EA as 'AND not OR' alongside Atlas. Hedgeye maintains long with $579 PT.

bullets.title: HPE: Record beat/raise on AI inferencing; Oracle partnership and AMD Helios upside not in guidance
bullets.body: HPE F3Q26 revenues of $12.21B beat $11.97B consensus; EPS of $1.11 beat $0.93 guidance. FY26 EPS raised to $3.75-$3.85 and FY27 revenue raised to 13-17% growth (from 8-12%). Cloud & AI revenue hit $9.04B with 17% operating margins (vs. 7% year-ago). Post-quarter, HPE signed a $3.5B traditional server inferencing deal with a hyperscaler and a gigawatt-scale Oracle networking agreement (warrants issued). AMD Helios white-label switch opportunity estimated at 'tens of billions' not yet in guidance. Citi raised to Buy with $76 PT; JPM maintained OW at $70.

bullets.title: TTD: 15% RIF; Citi maintains Sell at $11 PT on multi-quarter lag before new products drive growth
bullets.body: Trade Desk announced an ~15% workforce reduction (~576 positions) in Q3 2026, with estimated $86-115M in annualized savings. Q3 EBITDA margin guided at 24.6% (-1,830bps YoY), with management targeting 40%+ long-term margins. Citi maintains Sell at $11 PT (5x '27E EV/EBITDA), citing execution headwinds from Red Canary transition, sales leadership turnover, and weak NNARR growth. New products (Measurement, Audience Unlimited, Zuma) need several quarters to drive durable growth.

bullets.title: NFLX: Price hikes in UK, Germany, Austria—estimated 2.5% firm-wide ARPU uplift
bullets.body: Netflix announced price increases across the UK (Standard with Ads +33%, Premium +11%) and Germany/Austria affecting ~36% of EMEA subs and ~12% of total subs. Citi estimates ~7.5% EMEA ARPU uplift and ~2.5% firm-wide ARPU benefit. German/Austrian consumer protection laws require affirmative consent, likely delaying benefits to FY27 for some tiers. Ad-tier price hikes are substantial (33-40%) intended to mitigate adverse mix shift. Citi maintains Buy at $100 PT (21% upside from $82.67).

bullets.title: CRM: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform; Agentforce at $1.5B ARR with consumption-based monetization accelerating
bullets.body: Wolfe upgrades Salesforce to Outperform citing Agentforce ARR of $1.5B (+200% YoY), 50% of Q2 bookings from customers buying more credits after initial allotment, and AWUs up 97% QoQ. Service use cases consume ~5x more AWUs than other applications. Salesforce is enabling outcome-based pricing (per-lead, per-resolution) as next monetization leg. CRM is Citi's top pick in software 2H26 playbook alongside MDB, ORCL, SNOW, TEAM, and FIG.

bullets.title: CRWD: Fal.Con '26 raises FY28 NNARR guide to 20%+ (vs. 11% consensus); SafeMind and Falcon Guardian launched
bullets.body: CrowdStrike accelerated its $10B ARR target to FY30 (from FY31) and $20B to FY35 (from FY36). FY28 NNARR growth guided at 20%+ vs. consensus of ~11-14%. New product launches at Fal.Con include Falcon Guardian (full lifecycle AI agent security) and SafeMind (closed-loop agentic security models) priced via token-based Falcon Flex. Citi maintains Buy at $260 PT; ROTH raised to $220; Mizuho raised to $250. Agentic security TAM modeled at $215B by FY35.

bullets.title: UBER: 10% RIF (~3.3K positions) to fund AV programs; AI-driven efficiency frees capital
bullets.body: Uber announced a 10% global workforce reduction (~3.3K employees) to streamline management layers, reduce single/two-person teams, and reallocate savings toward autonomous vehicle programs and growth initiatives. The company noted 70%+ of pull requests are AI-attributed and cost-per-session has fallen 52% from peak. Citi and MS Broadening Webcast noted UBER as a non-AI best idea. CVNA also highlighted as MS Overweight at $90 PT.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybercab launch in Austin with ~45 units registered; NHTSA investigation opened
bullets.body: Tesla officially launched Cybercab for public rides in Austin with approximately 45 registered units. The NHTSA opened an investigation into Cybercab self-certification. Morgan Stanley viewed the event as an important robotaxi milestone while Citi noted only 200+ unsupervised vehicles in the US fleet vs. Waymo's ~4,000 driverless units. Tesla stock declined ~5.9% following the Cybercab launch event, which investors viewed as underwhelming relative to expectations. Texas DMV data will be a key tracker of fleet expansion.

bullets.title: META: Upgraded to OW at Morgan Stanley; $17B settlement clears overhang; Hatch/MetaClaw AI catalyst imminent
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded META to Overweight with a $775 PT (bull case $1,000) citing the $17B bipartisan AG settlement as a legal clearing event and the imminent launch of Hatch (a social AI agent) and MetaClaw. MS estimates $10+ incremental EPS from AI agents, Watermelon model, subscriptions, and SMB tools. META trades at 16x forward EPS, ~25% below its long-term average. Hedgeye Risk Range shifted META to Bullish trend on Sept 4. Meta also launched Muse Spark 1.3, which outperformed GPT-5.6 Sol on coding benchmarks.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro pricing up $150-200; foldable at $2,399; production limited by quality yields
bullets.body: iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max expected to start at $1,249-$1,299/$1,349-$1,399 driven by 400% YoY increase in 256GB memory costs. The foldable iPhone Ultra is priced at ~$2,399 with ~7-8M C2H26 builds (20M first-gen cycle). Production of foldables is limited to a few hundred units per day due to quality inspection reject rates. Tim Cook's last day as CEO was August 31; John Ternus succeeded as CEO. September 9 event is next catalyst. KeyBanc rates Underweight at $250 PT; JPM OW with $100 price hike base case.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY OSB GGR -41% YoY for week ending 8/30 (calendar); 3QTD tracking +13%; Wolfe initiates OP
bullets.body: NY OSB GGR fell 41% YoY for the week ending 8/30 on the Week Zero vs. Week 1 football timing mismatch. Excluding Fanatics, down 34%. 3QTD NY OSB GGR is tracking +13% YoY with DraftKings at +13% handle share of ~35%. Wolfe Research initiated DraftKings as its top pick in the Gaming & Lodging initiation (Outperform, $40 PT) noting scale leadership and underappreciated prediction market costs/benefits.

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Citi bullish as AI/HPC demand drives 25% IT load CAGR; data center NIMBY risks contained
bullets.body: Citi forecasts global IT load CAGR of 25% from 121 GW in 2026 to 370 GW in 2031, driven by AI/HPC and agentic workloads. EQIX is Citi's top pick heading into the Global TMT Conference. Mizuho also remains bullish on both EQIX (OW, $1,275 PT) and DLR (OW, $223 PT) despite data center NIMBY legislation spreading across US states—existing permitted projects are insulated. Trump publicly endorsed data centers as economic drivers, potentially reducing political headwinds.

bullets.title: Lp(a)/pelacarsen failure pressures AMGN; CRSP pivots to higher-potency CTX321
bullets.body: Novartis's pelacarsen phase 3 HORIZON trial failed to reduce MACE-4 despite lowering Lp(a) in 8,323 CVD patients. AMGN's OCEAN(a)-Outcomes now faces elevated mechanistic risk for olpasiran, though differentiated by higher baseline Lp(a), siRNA vs. ASO mechanism, and deeper suppression (>90%). CRSP's gene editing program likely shifts priority from CTX320 to CTX321 (2x more potent), with a 2026 program update expected. Citi maintains CRSP Buy at $88 PT with 57.7% upside.
